entry.title: Bitcoin Core v31.2 Released
entry.summary:
Bitcoin Core has announced the release of version 31.2, which is now available for download at [https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-31.2/](https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-31.2/). This latest update features a range of bug fixes, performance enhancements, and updated translations. Users are encouraged to report any bugs through the issue tracker on GitHub at [https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues) or join discussions via [https://bitcoincore.org/en/list/announcements/join/](https://bitcoincore.org/en/list/announcements/join/).
To upgrade to this new version, users running an older instance should first shut it down completely before proceeding with the installation. For Windows systems, the installer can be executed directly, while macOS users should copy over the `/Applications/Bitcoin-Qt` directory. Linux users need to replace the `bin/` and `libexec/` directories. Upgrading from end-of-life (EOL) versions is supported but may require additional time if data migration is necessary. Older wallets remain generally compatible with this release.
Bitcoin Core 31.2 is officially supported and tested on Linux Kernel 3.17 and newer, macOS 14, and Windows 10 (version 1903) or later. While the software is expected to work on most Unix-like operating systems, these environments are not tested as rigorously, and use on unsupported platforms is not recommended.
Key changes in this release include the implementation of BIP 323, which reserves version bits 5 to 28 for extra nonce space, effectively ignoring these bits for soft fork signaling and suppressing warnings about unknown deployments when these bits are set in block versions. The private-broadcast queue, relevant for transactions submitted via `sendrawtransaction` with private broadcast enabled, is now limited to 10,000 entries. When this limit is reached, further submissions are rejected until space is freed using the `getprivatebroadcastinfo` and `abortprivatebroadcast` commands.
Several improvements target network stability, transaction propagation, and code maintainability. Updates include adjustments to peer-to-peer networking, validation routines, and exception monitoring, as well as enhanced handling of Tor examples and IPv6 documentation addresses. The build system has received patches to improve cross-platform compatibility, including specific changes for Darwin-based systems. Documentation updates provide clearer build guides and reference recent protocol improvements, such as deterministic ECDSA signatures with low-R grinding.
A number of contributors have been credited for their work on this release, reflecting broad collaboration within the community and significant input into translations. This release continues Bitcoin Core’s commitment to reliability, security, and ongoing enhancement of its core functionality.
